title: Glendale Reconstruction & Rebuild | Gold Water Fire | Phoenix, AZ
description: Reconstruction and rebuild after fire or water damage in Glendale, AZ. Gold Water Fire rebuilds drywall, cabinets, flooring and roofs. Call (480) 999-3339.
intro: The demolition is done and the fans are gone, and now you are standing in a house with studs showing and a tarp where the ceiling used to be. Maybe you have been living in two rooms of your own home for weeks, taping plastic over a doorway, moving boxes from one side of the garage to the other. It is a strange kind of tired: nothing is actively going wrong anymore, but nothing is finished either, and every day you walk past the same unfinished wall. That waiting stage wears people down more than the emergency did.

sections.heading: Putting a Glendale house back to the way it was
sections.body: Reconstruction is the second half of a damage claim, and it is a different trade from mitigation. Mitigation is about drying, cutting out wet material and cleaning smoke residue. Reconstruction is licensed construction work: framing where studs were cut away, new insulation and drywall, texture matched to the surrounding walls, paint, trim and baseboard, cabinets and countertops, flooring, doors, and often electrical and plumbing rough-in where lines were opened up. On a fire loss it can also mean sealing charred framing, replacing sheathing and roof decking, and rebuilding soffits and eaves. The part homeowners underestimate is matching. Glendale neighborhoods tend to be built in large tracts where every house on the street used the same cabinet line, the same 1990s knockdown texture, the same 12x12 tile. When that product is discontinued, the rebuild has to either find a close equivalent or work out a sensible break line, at a doorway or a change in flooring, so the repair does not read as a patch. Getting that decision right early saves an argument later. See our full Reconstruction & Rebuild page for how the phase is organized.

sections.heading: Why Glendale homes fail in particular ways
sections.body:
Glendale spans a wide range of building eras, and each one breaks differently. The older core near Downtown Glendale, Catlin Court and the streets around 59th and Glendale Avenue includes homes from the mid-century era and earlier: lath areas, original galvanized or early copper supply lines, evaporative cooler stands still sitting on roofs, and slab foundations with cast iron drains that scale shut over decades. When those drains back up, the water goes into the slab and under wood or laminate flooring rather than running to a drain.

The big Arrowhead Ranch, Sonoran Foothills-adjacent and north Glendale tracts around the 101 and Union Hills are largely 1980s through early 2000s construction: two-story plans with second-floor laundry rooms and upstairs bathrooms, polybutylene or early plastic supply lines in some phases, and multi-zone HVAC with air handlers in the attic. A failed washing machine hose or a condensate pan overflow on the second floor sends water down through the ceiling into the living room, which is why those losses so often turn into a rebuild of two floors, not one. Homes near the Agua Fria and New River channels, and the flatter west Glendale areas toward Litchfield Park and El Mirage, also sit where sheet flow collects during heavy rain.

Seasonally, the pattern is predictable. Monsoon storms from roughly July into September bring wind that lifts tile and strips flat-roof material off additions and patio rooms, then dumps rain into the opening the wind just made. Winter rain finds the same weak spots more slowly. And the long stretch of extreme heat cooks roof underlayment and dries out caulk and roof penetrations, so a roof that held last year may not hold this year.

sections.heading: Scope, insurance, and one crew that stays through the end
sections.body: A rebuild goes better when the scope is written down before demolition dust settles. That means a room-by-room list of what was removed and what has to go back, photos tied to each line, and material selections chosen early so long-lead items like cabinets and specialty tile are ordered instead of holding up the whole schedule. Most insurance carriers price repairs from a standard estimating platform, so the rebuild estimate should speak that same line-item language: not "repair kitchen" but the actual counts of drywall, texture, primer, finish coats, cabinet boxes and toe kick. At Gold Water Fire, reconstruction is led by Construction Manager Brandon Gurr, with Johnny as Reconstruction Team Lead running the work in the house. Brooke handles water and mitigation scheduling, and Kristine keeps paperwork and appointments straight in the office. Co-founders Jim Bennett and Jake Taylor built the company to carry both halves of a loss, mitigation and the rebuild, so you are not handing off from one company to another halfway through. We are licensed in Arizona under AZ ROC #264344, KB-2, and we work the full Phoenix metro area from Peoria in the northwest across to Avondale, out to San Tan Valley and Apache Junction, and further out as needed. More about the people doing the work is on our about page.

sections.heading: When the rebuild is not the first step yet
sections.body: If water is still standing, or the house still smells like smoke, the rebuild waits. Drying and cleaning have to finish first, and drywall closed over damp framing invites mold behind a brand new wall. Structural material needs to reach a dry standard before anything is rebuilt over it, verified with moisture readings rather than a guess about how long the fans ran. On fire losses, smoke odor lives in framing, insulation and ductwork, and sealing has to happen while surfaces are still open and reachable. If you are earlier in the process than you thought, start with water damage restoration or fire damage restoration, and the rebuild follows from the same file with the same people already familiar with your house.

faqs.q: Can you do the rebuild if another company did the demolition and drying?
faqs.a: Yes. We will walk the house, document what was removed, take moisture readings to confirm the structure is dry before we close anything up, and write a room-by-room scope for the repairs. If drying was not finished, we will tell you that before we hang drywall rather than after.

faqs.q: Will the new drywall texture and flooring match the rest of my Glendale house?
faqs.a: That is the goal, and it is a real conversation on tract-built homes. Knockdown and orange-peel textures can be matched closely by hand. Discontinued tile, cabinet doors and laminate planks sometimes cannot, so we look for a close equivalent or a natural break line at a doorway or flooring transition so the repair does not read as a patch.

faqs.q: Do you work directly with my insurance adjuster?
faqs.a: We write the rebuild scope in line-item detail with supporting photos so the adjuster can review it against the estimate, and we will talk through differences with them. You still control your claim and your choices, and we will explain what is covered scope versus an upgrade you are choosing yourself.

faqs.q: What parts of Glendale do you cover?
faqs.a: All of it, from Downtown Glendale and Catlin Court to Arrowhead Ranch and the north Glendale tracts along the 101, plus the west side toward El Mirage and Litchfield Park. Our service area runs across the Phoenix metro from Peoria in the northwest to Avondale in the southeast, out to San Tan Valley and Apache Junction, and outlying areas further than that.

cta.body: You have carried this far enough on your own. Call Gold Water Fire at (480) 999-3339 or email Help@goldwaterfire.com, and we will come look at what is left, write down what it takes to finish it, and give you one crew responsible for getting your Glendale home back together.
